summary: This note is an introduction to the history of the Los Angeles Rams, an NFL franchise. It traces the team from its 1936 founding as the Cleveland Rams through its 1946 move to Los Angeles, its 1995-2015 stint as the St. Louis Rams, and its 2016 return to Southern California. It also previews the article's focus on the franchise's Los Angeles-area years and venues.
one_line: Overview of the Los Angeles Rams NFL franchise's history, from its 1936 Cleveland founding through its Los Angeles, St. Louis and return eras.
key_facts: The Los Angeles Rams are a professional American football team that play in the National Football League (NFL).
The Rams franchise was founded in 1936 as the Cleveland Rams.
The Cleveland Rams played in the short-lived second American Football League before joining the NFL the next year.
In 1946, the franchise moved to Los Angeles.
The Rams franchise remained in the Los Angeles metro area until 1994, when they moved to St. Louis.
The team was known as the St. Louis Rams from 1995 to 2015.
The Rams franchise returned to Los Angeles in 2016.
From 1946 to 1979, the Rams played at the Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum.
From 1980 to 1994, the Rams played at Anaheim Stadium in Anaheim.
Anaheim Stadium is now known as Angel Stadium of Anaheim.
The article chronicles the franchise's history during its time in Los Angeles and its return to Southern California beginning with the 2016 season.
